subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Turner <aiden.turner@acme.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed next steps — technical deep dive

Hi Aiden / Maya,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the candid discussion about your latency and throughput challenges for the new in-app assistant. Quick recap of the items we discussed and proposed next steps: 

Pain points / goals
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for short-turn prompts (chat snippets)
- Sustained throughput target: ~50 requests/sec for QPS-heavy peaks, with spikes to 200 req/s during flash events
- Consistent streaming experience for partial responses and tool-calling
- Tight cost controls (unit economics) while maintaining quality similar to 7B-class models
- Data residency and auditability requirements (SOC 2 + KMS integration)

Model / deployment considerations we discussed
- Preferred model class: 7B–13B encoder-decoder or causal chat model (streaming + tool calling support)
- Primary deployment: Dedicated GPU pool (US-West) for predictable latency; fallback to hosted multi-tenant for burst capacity
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes (high hit-rate on assistant prompts)
- Recommend enabling 8-bit/quantized runtime paths for cost-sensitive workloads after validation

SLOs (initial asks)
- 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for < 512 token context
- 99th percentile tail <= 400ms for single-turn interactive use
- Sustained throughput capacity: 50 rps; burst handling up to ~200 rps with graceful degradation

Next steps
1) Technical deep dive with engineering — Priya (SE) and Dev (infra) from our side. Proposed slot: Tue, Dec 14, 2026, 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET.
2) We'll bring a short agenda (deployment topology options, telemetry requirements, sample payload sizing, and initial performance runbook).
3) I'll attach a short SLO template and a mutual action plan to capture timelines and procurement touch points.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx; SLO_requirements_template.xlsx (stubs)

Please confirm the proposed time or suggest alternatives. Also, if you can share a representative payload size (avg/95p token counts) and expected percent of streaming responses, that will help us prepare.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed next steps — technical deep dive

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. High level confirmation and a few clarifying items from our side: 

- Latency targets look right — 200ms p95 is what our PM org is asking for. The hardest part will be keeping p95 stable under the 200 rps bursts; curious how you recommend fallbacks behave.
- Concurrency details: our average payload is ~1.2KB (text-only, about ~200 tokens), 95p is ~3.5KB. We expect ~65% of responses to use streaming (progressive replies / tool hints).
- Procurement timeline: we’re targeting Q1 production (contracts signed by end of Jan).
- Compliance: we need clear details on KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) and egress restrictions for EU data — will that come up in the deep dive?

I can confirm one of the proposed slots — Dec 14 at 2:00 PM PT (we're on Pacific). That works better for our infra lead. Can you confirm and include a calendar invite?

Looping in Priya from Redwood so she can scope the tech session and Dev (infra) if helpful. Also looping Maya (PM) for timelines.

Thanks,
Aiden
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
aiden.turner@acme.com

Thanks Aiden — welcome, Maya.

I’ll run the technical deep dive on Dec 14 at 2:00 PM PT. High-level agenda I’ll cover:
- Confirming exact SLO definitions (p95/p99 measurement windows and how we measure tail latency)
- Model options and expected perf (7B vs 13B tradeoffs, quantization impact)
- Deployment topology: Dedicated pool + hosted fallback, cross-region routing, and KV cache placement
- Telemetry & tracing: required metrics (per-route latency, token-level cost, cache hit-rates) and what we need from your side (sample payloads, expected request/second profile)
- Security & compliance: BYOK KMS flows, audit log retention, VPC peering/network egress considerations
- Next steps: perf validation plan (load profile, test dataset), mutual action plan milestones, and procurement handoff

What would be most helpful before the session:
- Representative sample payloads (one short chat, one long prompt) — for perf runs
- Expected concurrent sessions during peak flash events (even rough numbers)
- Any internal egress restrictions for EU data (if you have policy docs, share links)

I’ll attach a short agenda and send a calendar invite. If you prefer an earlier slot on Dec 14 (10am PT) instead of 2pm, let me know — otherwise I’ll keep 2pm as confirmed.
